species.real: Lough Neagh runs the largest wild eel fishery in Europe as a fishermen's co-operative, and Lough Neagh eels have protected PGI status, like Champagne or Parma ham.
species.name: Neagheen

dex.text: A wee yellow-bellied eel that lives in the lough mud for years, growing slowly and saying nothing. The -een on the end means small in Irish English; it becomes Neaghmor, mór being Irish for big. It has already swum further than you ever will.
dex.fact: European eels hatch in the Sargasso Sea and drift thousands of miles to Europe as see-through glass eels, then spend years in fresh water as yellow eels; Lough Neagh's wild eels have had EU Protected Geographical Indication status since 2011.

species.real: Legend says Fionn mac Cumhaill made Lough Neagh by scooping up a clod of earth to throw at a rival, and the clod landed in the sea as the Isle of Man.
species.name: Neaghmor

dex.text: The great silver eel of the lough, as long as a rowing boat and twice as stubborn. Old fishermen say it lives in the hole Finn McCool left behind, and on wild nights it goes looking for the sea.
dex.fact: Grown eels turn silver before their last journey, and they leave Lough Neagh for the sea on dark, moonless, stormy autumn nights, heading back to the Sargasso Sea to spawn.
